prerequisites: Previous knowledge of Graphic Expression is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Interpret and represent assembly and detail drawings of mechanisms, structures, and installations.
Master and proficiently use parametric drawing software.
Determine operating conditions of common parts in mechanisms and the relationship between them.
Correctly use specifications, regulations, and mandatory graphic representation standards.
Understand the industrial design method and its working tools.

syllabus_topics: Module 1: Parametric modeling of mechanical elements
Topic M02: Installation, environment, and project management in Autodesk Inventor.
Topic M03: Sketches, constraints, and dimensions.
Topic M08: Libraries of standardized parts.
Topic M10: Design assistants I: shafts, keys, bearings, pins.
Topic M11: Design assistants II: gears, springs, belts, and chains.
Topic M12: Other environments: Welding, Sheet metal parts.
Topic T01: Assembly and detail drawings.
Topic T03: Dimensional tolerances and fits.
Topic T05: Dimensioning and functional analysis.
Topic T07: Shafts and axles, keys and pins.
Topic T10: Other transmission elements: belts and chains.
Topic T11: Fixed connections: rivets and welding.

assessment_methods.method: Active participation (expository classes and laboratory practices) (EV4)

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, students must attend at least 80% of practical classes (both classroom and laboratory practices). The final grade is calculated as 0.2 x EV1 + 0.3 x EV2 + 0.3 x EV3 + 0.2 x EV4. EV1 and EV3 require a minimum of 50% of their maximum score to be considered passed. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For extraordinary evaluation, students must retake EV1 and/or EV3; if EV2 was not passed, an individual assignment will be provided.
